init.title: LG webOS Remote options
init.description:
Moving the TV cursor (pointer mode and air pointer) sends a lot of small messages. By default they travel through Home Assistant's normal connection, which can make the cursor stutter when Home Assistant is busy or the phone is on a slow link.

The low-latency side channel is an optional shortcut: Home Assistant opens a second, secure (https) port that only handles cursor moves and passes them straight to the TV. The card uses it automatically and quietly falls back to the normal connection if it cannot connect, so leaving this on is safe.

It only starts when Home Assistant itself serves https (an SSL certificate in the `http:` settings). Behind a reverse proxy or when using Nabu Casa remote access it does not start, and the normal connection is used. Your phone must be able to reach the port (same network, or the port forwarded). Changes apply after a restart.

data_description.side_channel: On: smoother cursor when the side channel can start and your phone can reach it. Off: always use Home Assistant's normal connection (slightly less smooth, nothing extra to open).
data_description.side_port: TCP port for the second https connection (default 8124). Change it only if another service already uses 8124. Open or forward the same port if you use the card away from home.
